walkthroughs.body_html:
Rate = how fast the reaction goes.

You can measure it as the amount of product made per second — e.g. gas volume per second.

Or as the amount of reactant used per second — e.g. mass lost per second.

A bigger number = faster reaction. A flat line on a graph means the reaction has finished.

For a reaction to happen, particles must collide. But not just any collision will do.

The collision needs enough energy — at least the activation energy. Otherwise particles bounce off unreacted.

More collisions per second and more of them being successful = a faster rate.

Temperature ↑: particles move faster, collide more often, and more collisions reach the activation energy.

Concentration ↑: more particles in the same volume, so more collisions per second.

Surface area ↑: powder reacts faster than a lump — more particles exposed.

Catalyst: provides a different route with lower activation energy. Not used up.

mcqs.q: According to collision theory, a successful collision needs.
options: Any contact at all
At least the activation energy
A catalyst always
The particles to be the same element

mcqs.q: Powdered marble chips react faster with acid than large lumps because.
options: The powder is more concentrated
The powder has a larger surface area exposed
The powder is hotter
Lumps absorb the acid

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
Higher temperature increases the concentration of the reactants.

mcqs.q: Why does increasing temperature increase the rate of reaction significantly?
options: Particles collide much more frequently at higher temperature, which is the main reason for the rate increase.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
Mainly because a much larger fraction of collisions have energy at least equal to the activation energy; collision frequency increases only slightly.
Higher temperature increases the concentration of the reactants.

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: Higher temperature increases the concentration of the reactants.
Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.
Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
